properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 22 at 7:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 700 AM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Sand Hollow State Park, or 24 miles southwest of Zion National Park,
moving north at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Washington, Hurricane, Quail Creek State Park, Sand Hollow State
Park, Toquerville, Leeds and Pintura.

This includes Interstate 15 between mile markers 15 and 34.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Very heavy rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM WILL IMPACT CENTRAL WASHINGTON COUNTY UNTIL 730 AM MDT

properties.areaDesc: Eastern San Gabriel Mountains
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 22 at 5:58AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:

Glendora, moving north at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Wrightwood...
Glendora...
Falling Springs...
Bridge Burn Scar...
Angeles Crest Highway between Mount Waterman and
Wrightwood...
and Big Pines.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Persons in campgrounds should consider seeking sturdy shelter until
this storm passes.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 5:48AM PDT until October 22 at 8:45AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of Eastern Los Angeles County in southwestern
California...

* WHEN...Until 845 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 547 AM PDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small
stream flooding. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pomona, San Dimas, Glendora, La Verne, Claremont, Diamond Bar and
Walnut.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Gila, AZ
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:48AM MST until October 22 at 8:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 548 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Sycamore Burn Scar. Up to 0.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Sycamore Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Sycamore Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Gila County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Sycamore Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 5:38AM PDT until October 22 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall from storms
training over the same area.

* WHERE...A portion of central California, including the following
areas, Bakersfield, Buena Vista, Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5,
Frazier Mountain Communities, Grapevine, Indian Wells Valley, Kern
River Valley, Mojave Desert, Mojave Desert Slopes, Piute Walker
Basin, South End San Joaquin Valley, Tehachapi and West Side
Mountains South of 198.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become
clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong area of low pressure off the Southern California coast
will move inland and interact with tropical moisture.
- Be especially careful on Highway 58 between mile markers 101 to
103 and the Borel burn scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 22 at 5:37AM PDT until October 22 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...There is an 70% chance of 4 inches or more of snow along the
Tioga Pass and highway 120. There is a 60-80% chance for four
inches or more of snow above 8,000 feet in Tulare, Madera, and
Fresno Counties.

* WHERE...Above 8,000 feet in the Sierra Nevada.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous.

driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.description:

* WHERE...West Central San Luis Obispo County in southwestern
California...

* WHEN...Until 815 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

and thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Morro Bay, Baywood-Los Osos, Diablo Canyon, Avila Beach, Cayucos

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.areaDesc: Garfield, UT; Kane, UT; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 6:16AM MDT until October 22 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is occurring.
Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue
trough this evening. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow rapidly increasing flows across all waterways within the
warned area, including all of the Glen Canyon National Recreation
Area. Increasingly high flows are expected in, but not limited
to...the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek, Last Chance Creek,
Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and tributaries. Many
backcountry roads within this area are expected to become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 610 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen across the headwaters of the
Paria River, Escalante River, Wahweap Creek and other drainages
within the warned area. The Paria River at Highway 89 saw a peak
flow of nearly 2500 CFS overnight, while the Escalante River just
downstream from Escalante recorded a peak stage of 6 feet. These
flood waves will continue to move downstream through the morning
hours.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches are possible
through this evening. This will result in continued high flows
and additional flooding of all rivers, streams and normally dry
washes within the warned area.
- Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, including the Escalante
region. Kodachrome State Park, Tropic, Cannonville, Escalante,
and Big Water
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks can become unstable and
unsafe.
